title: Firmware: RFC 8628 pairing + device token — the gate for everything relay-side
description:
THE BLOCKER for the entire phone-relay feature. Verified 2026-08-04: firmware/main/net_task.c sets exactly one header on its /v1/nearby POST (Content-Type). No Authorization. So every board resolves ANONYMOUSLY, the phone provider requires a device credential carrying read:fix, and the relay is unreachable from the only device that exists — no matter what the server holds.

Second blocker in the same file, line ~150: with a loc_set/CONFIG_GC_DEV_FIXED_LAT override active the board builds /v1/nearby?lat=..&lon=.. and supplies coordinates itself, bypassing server-side resolution entirely. Testing the relay requires loc_clear first.

Server side is done and deployed (M2 PR #13, M3 PR #14). What the firmware owes:

1. Pairing (RFC 8628, api/src/routes/pair.ts): POST /v1/device/pair/start, display ONLY the 8-char user_code as XXXX-XXXX, poll /v1/device/pair/poll on the advertised interval until it returns the token. The device_code is secret and never shown. Codes expire in 5 minutes.
2. Store the token in NVS. It is prefixed gtfsc_dev_. Note the guiding spec's flash-encryption caveat: extraction is easy today, which is why scopes are narrow and read:fix defaults off.
3. Send it as 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' on /v1/nearby (and /v1/locate if used). Never as a query param — the server rejects that by design.
4. Handle 401 (revoked/unknown token) by dropping to anonymous rather than failing hard, and surfacing 'unpaired' on screen. Unpair is a user action from the config UI and must not brick the board.
5. A rotation response header is specified but unimplemented server-side; ignore it for now, it exists so adopting it later is not a breaking change.

Only after this does gc-x8n.4 (rendering quality/captured_at) have anything to render, and only then does gc-cls (freshness instrumentation) read anything but zeros.

Worth planning together with gc-g6f (M3 power model): how often the board wakes determines how fresh a relayed fix has to be, and both assumptions have to agree.

title: AE6d read side: locate chain must skip the phone provider once read:fix is revoked (U8)
description:
U10 landed the stored-state half of AE6d: revoking `read:fix` (and unpairing) calls `clearFix(deviceId)` in `api/src/relay.ts`, so the delivered position is deleted, and `api/test/workers/config.test.ts` proves it against `device_fixes`.

The read-side half is NOT implemented and is deliberately left as an `it.todo` in that file rather than a vacuously-passing test: R9 also requires that the locate chain skip the phone provider unless the resolved credential *currently* carries `read:fix`. That cannot exist until U8 splits the chain and adds the phone provider (`locate.ts` today resolves WiFi -> unknown and has no per-credential context).

Done when: U8's `resolveLocation(ctx)` consults the credential's live scopes, and a test shows a device whose grant was revoked resolves `/v1/locate` and `/v1/nearby` without the phone provider even if a fix row were present. Replace the `it.todo` in api/test/workers/config.test.ts (or move it to the locate suite).

title: Set Phase 5 Worker secrets (Resend + allowlist + public origin)
description: Five settings, all via 'cd api && npx wrangler secret put <NAME>' so nothing lands in shell history or a transcript, and so wrangler.jsonc stays generic for forks: RESEND_API_KEY (secret), AUTH_EMAIL_PROVIDER=resend, AUTH_EMAIL_FROM=signin@<domain verified with Resend>, AUTH_ALLOWED_EMAILS=<Mario's address>, AUTH_PUBLIC_ORIGIN=https://gtfs-compass-api.<subdomain>.workers.dev. AUTH_ALLOWED_EMAILS is the one that matters for safety: unset means sign-up is open to anyone who can reach the Worker (that is R4b's specified default and it logs a warning, but it is not what you want). AUTH_PUBLIC_ORIGIN was a security-review finding — unset, the emailed link's origin is derived from whatever Host the request carried. Sign-in fails closed until the provider is configured, so there is no half-open window.

title: Instrument relay freshness-at-read so the posting-cadence question is measurable
description:
Mario wants to evaluate posting strategies (Shortcut automations vs a background app) empirically rather than by feel, on criteria of freshness, coverage and battery. The server already knows the number that matters and throws it away.

The metric: when a board reads the relay, how old was the fix? getFix computes ageS on every read and uses it only to pick current vs last_known. Bucketing it would answer 'did the phone's posting strategy have something useful there when the device actually asked' — which is the whole question, and is not answerable today.

Proposed shape: a sharded auth_budgets-style counter keyed by bucket — absent / <=120s (current) / <=15m / <=1h / <=4h (the last_known ceiling) — incremented in the composer when the phone provider is consulted. No coordinates, no timestamps per read, so it adds no location data at rest; it is a histogram of staleness. Reuses readBudget/incrementBudget and needs no new table.

Note the F6 fix deliberately stopped persisting phone-sourced resolutions into locate_log, so that table is NOT the place for this — a counter is, and it is also the privacy-preserving option.

Also worth capturing: coverage (reads where the phone provider produced nothing and the chain fell through) is the same counter's 'absent' bucket, so one addition answers both freshness and coverage.

Blocked in practice until the firmware sends a device token (gc-x8n.4) — before that every board resolves anonymously and never consults the relay, so the counter would read all zeros.

title: Decide the phone's relay credential: session vs a write:fix phone token
description:
M3 shipped the relay as session-only: relay:true requires a session because putFixForUser takes a user, and a session is what names one. That is browser-shaped — a __Host- cookie, the X-GC-CSRF header, and a same-origin Origin.

A native or Shortcut client CAN satisfy all three (iOS persists cookies in the native store; both headers are settable), so a phone-side MVP needs no API change. But it is fragile in exactly the way that matters here: a session silently expiring means location quietly stops flowing with nothing on screen to notice, and the failure is invisible until the board shows a stale position.

The cleaner answer reuses what M2 already built: mint a phone credential through the RFC 8628 pairing flow with a write:fix scope instead of read:fix. authorize() already fails closed for non-session credentials unless a route names a scope, so the seam exists — it is one scope, one route branch, and a decision about whether a phone is a 'device' in the devices table or a new kind.

DECISION NEEDED FROM MARIO, not a foregone conclusion. Cost of the token path: a schema/scope change and a second pairing UX on the phone. Cost of the session path: nothing now, fragility later. Recommendation: build the phone MVP against the session first so we learn whether background posting actually helps; if it does, do this properly through ce-plan rather than hardening the workaround.

title: Firmware: store multiple WiFi networks so the board auto-joins home/work/hotspot
description:
From Mario's own Phase 5 scoping note on gc-x8n: 'store multiple WiFi networks (home/work/hotspot) so auto-join works wherever known WiFi exists.' It never made it into any of Phase 5's units (M1-M5 are all server-side) and is not otherwise tracked.

Why it matters now: M3 shipped the phone relay, which solves LOCATION but explicitly not DATA — the board still fetches its own JSON over its own network. So in the field it depends on joining a network, and today the firmware seeds a single SSID/password into NVS (console 'wifi_set', or the CONFIG_GC_WIFI_SSID/PASSWORD build-time seed). One credential means the board works at home OR on the hotspot, not both without re-provisioning.

Shape: NVS list rather than a single pair, join by best available, console command to add/remove/list. Firmware-only; no API change. Independent of the BLE data-mule path (which would remove the data dependence entirely and is Phase 6-ish), so this is worth having regardless of whether that ever lands.

title: firmware: render provider and age from the locate wire's quality/captured_at (R13)
description:
U8 added two device-facing fields to the locate wire. Both /v1/locate and /v1/nearby's `location` object now carry, ONLY when the position came from the relayed phone fix:

  provider: "phone"
  captured_at: <epoch seconds the phone fixed the position>
  quality: "current" | "last_known"

Absent fields mean a WiFi-resolved (or GET-supplied) position, which is the shipped behavior byte for byte — a firmware that ignores the new keys keeps working, so this is additive, not breaking.

Done when the board renders 'via phone, 3 min ago' for quality:last_known (relative age from captured_at) rather than showing the coordinates as current. quality:current renders as today. Per R13 a last-known fix is a distinct state, not a position with an old timestamp.

Context: api/src/locate.ts (ResolvedLocation), README 'POST /v1/locate'.

title: Phase 4 M3: IMU wake, deep sleep, power model
description: QMI8658 wake-on-motion, deep sleep between glances, PWR button, AXP2101 rail management — the guiding spec's power model. After M2.
notes:
COUPLED TO THE PHONE RELAY — plan these together, not in sequence. M3 (PR 
#14) shipped a relay whose freshness model assumes something about how often
the board asks for a position: a fix reads as 'current' inside 120s and is 
refused entirely past a 4-hour ceiling. The wake cadence this epic chooses 
is what decides whether the relay usually has something useful when the 
board looks. 
 
The two designs have to agree on one question: does the board wake often 
enough that a movement-triggered phone post (iOS significant-location- 
change, or a Shortcut automation on leaving home) will normally have landed 
first? Mario's stated goals are motion-activated rather than always-polling,
minimal phone battery, and not having to pull the phone out at all — which 
points at movement-triggered posting on the phone side rather than a 
heartbeat, and makes the board's wake pattern the other half of the same 
decision. 
 
Also blocked-by in practice: gc-0u6 (firmware pairing + device token). Until
the board sends a credential it resolves anonymously and never consults the 
relay, so any power-model measurement taken before that will not reflect the
real request pattern (an authenticated /v1/nearby costs extra D1 reads and a
possible last_used_at write). 

WAKE-CADENCE CONTRACT PINNED (2026-08-04, gc-0u6 plan): docs/plans/2026-08-04-001-feat-firmware-pairing-device-token-plan.md 'Wake-Cadence / Freshness Contract' section is the shared reference — relay constants FIX_HORIZON_S=120s / FIX_LAST_KNOWN_MAX_AGE_S=4h (api/src/relay.ts, now also in CONCEPTS.md Fix Quality). M3's wake pattern must not assume the phone posts on a schedule; a movement-triggered glance usually finds last_known, rendered with honest age (gc-x8n.4). Power measurements before gc-0u6's PR merges+deploys still won't reflect authenticated request costs.

title: Reject a negative accuracy at the relay ingress (400)
description: M3 review residual. withinAccuracyGate now rejects accuracy < 0, so a negative value can never be SERVED. But a stored accuracy_m of -1 is still 'strictly more accurate' than every honest reading in putFixForUser's upsert predicate, so it blocks replacement for the full 120s horizon and the relay goes quiet for that device. Adding a write-side accuracy check inside relay.ts would contradict R12 (the accuracy gate is deliberately read-side only), so the right home is ingress validation in routes/locate.ts's readCapturedAt sibling: reject accuracy < 0 with a 400 alongside the existing lat/lon range checks. Blast radius is the poster's own devices, hence P3.

title: Confirm the relay's accuracy refinement is right for a walking user (U7 shipped it)
description:
U7 shipped the plan's refinement on latest-wins: a new fix does not replace a strictly more accurate one still inside the 120 s horizon (api/src/relay.ts, putFixForUser's upsert WHERE). Intended case: a phone that momentarily falls back to cell-tower accuracy must not erase the good GPS position the device is about to read.

Consequence to confirm (already flagged as an open question in docs/plans/2026-08-03-004, Open Questions): a *walking* user whose GPS accuracy genuinely degrades keeps an older position for up to two minutes. Nothing is mislabeled — getFix reports capturedAt/ageS/quality honestly, and past the horizon the stored fix is outranked by anything current — but the position lags.

If Mario wants both cases covered, the plan's own suggestion is a 'not more than 30 s older' clause: let the newer fix win regardless of accuracy once it is more than ~30 s newer than the stored one. That is a one-predicate change inside relay.ts plus a test; deliberately not taken in U7 because the plan specified exactly one refinement.

title: Retention sweep deletes device_fixes with direct SQL, outside the relay seam
description:
Plan Definition of Done: 'no SQL touches device_fixes outside the relay seam' — the property that keeps the documented D1->DO relay upgrade a three-function change. `api/src/retention.ts` (U11, shipped before `relay.ts` existed) issues its own `DELETE FROM device_fixes WHERE captured_at < ?` for the R20 sweep.

Not a bug today; it becomes one the moment the relay moves off D1, because the sweep would silently stop reaping anything. Fix: add `sweepStaleFixes(env, olderThanS, limit)` to `api/src/relay.ts` and have retention call it. Best done in U7, which is already opening that file.
notes: Still open and still accurate: retention.ts issues its own DELETE FROM device_fixes, so the plan's DoD ('no SQL touches device_fixes outside the relay seam') is unmet and a D1→DO swap would leave the sweep pointing at a table that no longer holds the data. The M2 review fix touched retention's auth_budgets sweep (a RETAINED_BUDGET_SCOPES list covering send:failure and the two pairing refusal counters) — unrelated to this. Right home is U7, which already opens relay.ts: add a purgeFixesOlderThan(env, cutoff, limit) export and have runRetentionPurge call it.
close_reason: Closed in U7: relay.ts now exports purgeFixesOlderThan(env, cutoffS, limit) — one bounded batch, returns rows deleted. retention.ts imports it and drives it through a new repeatBounded() helper (purgeInBatches refactored to sit on top of it), so batching, the maxBatches budget, pending accounting and the maintenance_runs bookkeeping are unchanged. grep now shows the only SQL against device_fixes in api/src is in relay.ts. Existing retention tests pass untouched, including the drop-table failure test.
